description:
A psychology graduate student needs to verify the Big Five factor structure of their BFI-25 survey data before computing composite personality scores. Open the BFI25.csv dataset (already loaded in Jamovi from ~/Documents/Jamovi/BFI25.csv), which contains 25 personality items (A1-A5, C1-C5, E1-E5, N1-N5, O1-O5) rated on a 1-6 Likert scale by ~2,236 participants, plus gender and age columns.

Perform the following steps:

1. Ensure all 25 item variables (A1 through O5) are set to **Continuous** measurement type (they may be auto-detected as Ordinal). Do NOT include gender or age in the analysis.

2. Run a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) — NOT Exploratory Factor Analysis — via Analyses > Factor > Principal Component Analysis.

3. Move all 25 item variables (A1-A5, C1-C5, E1-E5, N1-N5, O1-O5) into the Variables box.

4. Set the number of components to a **fixed number** of 5.

5. Set the rotation method to **Varimax**.

6. Under Additional Output, enable: **Component summary** (eigenvalues and variance) and **Scree plot**.

7. Set 'Hide loadings below' to 0.3.

8. Save the Jamovi project as `~/Documents/Jamovi/BFI25_PCA.omv`.

9. Create a plain-text report file at `~/Documents/Jamovi/pca_report.txt` containing exactly these three lines with values read from the Jamovi PCA output:

Cumulative Variance Explained (%): <value>
Component 1 Eigenvalue: <value>
Components with Eigenvalue > 1: <count>

Example format:
Cumulative Variance Explained (%): 44.3
Component 1 Eigenvalue: 4.87
Components with Eigenvalue > 1: 6
